original_prompt: After nine years before Troy, in the tenth campaigning season, the Achaeans remain unable to take the city. Hector and Achilles live. Following a storm, a smith and Odysseus investigate a damaged divine object, undertake an expedition, bargain for a small finite cache of firearms made by Hephaestus, and bring it back. Rival leaders debate its use; a crisis forces the first constrained deployment. Tell exactly four developed scenes: discovery without possession; expedition and costly acquisition; trial and contested counsel; first battle use and local climax. This is the opening movement of a larger alternate Trojan epic, not the fall of Troy. The weapons must be earned through buildup. Use elevated English shaped by Homeric epic and an ancient social imagination throughout. RETELL FROM SCRATCH: purely third person, no dialogue, no invocation. Four developed scenes, not a summary. Material causality and costly decisions carry character depth.
refined_prompt: After nine years of siege, the Achaeans are still outside Troy. Hector and Achilles survive. A storm damages a divine object, prompting a smith and Odysseus to investigate and undertake an expedition to a concealed coastal sanctuary. They acquire a cache of six cumbersome single-shot firearms made by Hephaestus. Rival leaders debate their use; a crisis forces the first constrained deployment. Develop exactly four scenes: the discovery of the damaged object; the expedition and acquisition of the cache; a trial and contested counsel; and the first battle use and local climax. This is the opening movement of a larger alternate Trojan epic, not the fall of Troy. The weapons must be earned through buildup. Use elevated English shaped by Homeric epic and an ancient social imagination throughout. RETELL FROM SCRATCH: purely third person, no dialogue, no invocation. Four developed scenes, not a summary. Material causality and costly decisions carry character depth.
central_conflict: The Achaeans must earn the cache of unfamiliar firearms through a costly expedition and bargaining process, while rival leaders debate their use and a crisis forces the first constrained deployment.
reader_experience: Wonder, anticipation, competing loyalties, martial terror and a costly local victory that opens a larger epic.

arc.costly_choice: Authorize first use despite a limitation he understands.
arc.old_strategy: Ask, test, bargain and reveal only what wins cooperation.
arc.possible_change: Gaining possession is different from controlling consequences.
arc.pressure_test: The bargain binds him to an obligation he cannot safely disclose.
arc.starting_belief: A useful advantage can be mastered through foresight.

contradiction.tension: He sees the costs hidden in heroic boasting while concealing the costs of his own bargains.

emotional_behavior.under_pressure: Becomes exact about names, objects and promises.

characters.fear: Returning with neither victory nor the men entrusted to him.

world_constraints.divine_framework: Hephaestus made the weapons for a divine purpose. A particular grievance and bargain explain access; no arbitrary delivery from the sky.
world_constraints.institutions: Achaean coalition of rival kings; command does not erase obligations or consent.
world_constraints.physical_systems: Greek shore and ships, storm-damaged coast, concealed coastal forge, trial ground and contested approach to Troy.
world_constraints.source_continuity: Tenth campaigning season before principal Iliad deaths; this new sequence is explicit alternate continuity, not a claimed canonical event.
world_constraints.technology: Cache: exactly six cumbersome single-shot weapons, with a finite supply of prepared charges explicitly fixed at acquisition. No resupply or reproduction within this arc.
world_constraints.track: Track each weapon, custodian, condition, remaining charges, travel, wounds, witnessed facts and private bargains.

suggested_techniques.guidance: Roughly one extended comparison per scene when earned, no mandatory quota. Let its image develop before returning to action. No modern image domains or continuous ornament.
